sparse_owned_batches.design: Packing state belongs to the result owner; small slabs grow geometrically from actual copied demand. Optional spare capacity falls back to exact-size storage. Published values never move.

warm_single_directory_points.design: Single-run lookups retain the established block loader and direct large-value lease adoption. With multiple overlapping runs, warm deciding candidates stop read-order traversal immediately; cold candidates prepare bounded asynchronous windows, consume results in visibility order and cancel remaining speculative reads after a deciding result. Preserve the bounds-index planner for unsupported directories or L0 counts greater than 64.
warm_single_directory_points.limitations: Synthetic maximum supported L0 overlap, latest-run hits, warm MemoryStorage, Debug. This does not establish end-to-end speedup.

design: Propagate explicit transaction-owned versus snapshot-pinned lifetime to single-key directory reads.
Use temporary block pins for ordinary probe fallback loaders and clear their borrowed legacy hints before releasing those pins.
Adopt decoder-owned results and recognize the active packed buffer in constant time, including reuse across lookups; inspect only new allocations for other interior slices.

ordinary_probe_ownership_followup.limitations: Payload buffer counts exclude metadata and storage/cache construction. No standalone speedup is claimed for cursor reuse; timing samples vary and do not establish end-to-end throughput or soak behavior.

design: Null pin ownership expresses transaction-owned results throughout synchronous and planned point loaders; copy into result storage before releasing the cache handle.

owned_fallback_policy_followup.limitations: Backend allocation counts exclude the result scratch allocator. Payload buffer counts exclude metadata and storage/cache construction. local_prefix.scope: MemoryStorage, prefix-compressed block, local/global decoded caches disabled, 128 distinct 80-byte keys, one-byte values. Backend allocation counter excludes result allocator. Compare legacy owned-entry decoder with direct-to-result output; metadata/workspace prewarmed.

dense_indexed_points.scope: One uncompressed indexed block, sorted distinct keys. Test-only row-parse counter; baseline clears cursor per key. Backward, duplicate, sparse, missing and namespace probes checked against the existing binary-search oracle.

shared_decoded_scratch.scope: Synthetic valid Snappy payload; counts decode-buffer allocation requests with and without workspace reuse, excluding payload generation and result copying.

shared_prefix_scratch.scope: Prefix-compressed table payload, 80-byte keys; shared decompression and reconstructed-key storage. Allocation-failure inventory uses no-resize allocator.

design: Emit local prefix point values directly into result-owner packing while preserving existing warm local leases and promotion.
Bind adaptive row readers to immutable shared block owners. Forward probes walk at most eight rows before binary search; backward probes seek and duplicate probes reuse the current row.
Acquire shared scratch workspace lazily from an independent four-slot pool. Physical arena capacity is bounded at 768 KiB per active batch; retain at most 64 KiB per idle slot plus arena headers.

Optional decode and small-key workspace exhaustion falls back to separately admitted mandatory scratch. Large keys retain existing scratch handling. Release shared block readers before resetting workspace.
Rebind idle workspace backing/manager by releasing old buffers and admission credit outside the coordination lock.
dense_prefix_scratch_followup.limitations: Debug helper measurements do not establish end-to-end throughput or 2 GiB soak behavior. A batch may wait for one of four workspace slots. Arena non-LIFO churn can exhaust optional pooled capacity and use mandatory scratch; oversized batches may discard/reallocate excess capacity. Retained workspaces remain resource-accounted.
